title: Mitigating Global Feature Collapse in Graph ODEs via Hysteretic Topology Evolution
claim: Positive diffusion collapses features to one consensus; coupling dynamics with bistable, hysteretic topology evolution preserves cluster structure instead.
layout: 5 panels A–E, mixed grid; coupled-ODE loop at left, double-well and bar plots
description: A five-panel composite figure. Panel A (top left) shows two complete graphs: colored nodes at t0 turn uniformly gray at t_end. Between them an arrow is labeled 'time evolution', with annotations 'uniformly positive mixing' and 'single global attractor (consensus)'. The equation Ḣ = −(I−P(t))H is shown below, along with a note on the monostability trap (Thm 3.4). Panel B (bottom left) is a gray box with a feedback loop. A blue 'Feature Diffusion dH/dt' box and an orange 'Topology Evolution dU/dt' box are joined by arrows labeled F(H) and A(U). Panel C (top right) plots a double-well potential V(U) from insulated to connected. Red and blue dashed curves show the wells tilted by the force F. Panel D plots an S-shaped hysteresis curve with a shaded bistable region. Panel E is a bar chart of Laplacian eigenvalues λ0, λ1, ... with a large spectral gap at λk.
caption: HGODE mechanism and theory scope. (A) Positive irreducible or uniformly positive diffusion-style Graph ODEs contract to a rank-one consensus subspace in the long-time regime. (B) HGODE makes topology a dynamical state by coupling feature diffusion with edge-potential evolution. (C–D) A feature-conditioned force tilts a double-well landscape, polarizing candidate edges into connected/insulated phases with hysteretic memory. (E) Edge polarization can move propagation toward block-structured mixing; in the idealized limit this yields cluster-wise invariant subspaces (e.g., multiple near-zero Laplacian eigenvalues) instead of global consensus.
abstract: Graph neural ordinary differential equations provide continuous-time propagation on graphs, but their long-time behavior is largely determined by the asymptotic structure of the mixing operator. We show that diffusion-style Graph ODEs with positive irreducible mixing face a \emph{monostability trap}, where node features converge to a rank-one consensus subspace. This reveals a structural limitation of positive diffusion-style continuous graph propagation: within this consensus class, exact long-time avoidance requires changing the effective support; otherwise, smooth suppression should be interpreted as finite-horizon or metastable mitigation. We address this by introducing a \emph{hysteretic mechanism} for topology evolution, where candidate edges carry latent bistable potentials in a double-well landscape. A node-feature-conditioned force field evolves these potentials, and a smooth sigmoid gate converts them into differentiable propagation weights. We prove global consensus under the stated mixing assumptions and block-wise consensus under idealised support separation. For consensus-form dynamics, we further establish a finite-horizon perturbation bound under small cross-block leakage, and empirically evaluate the resulting nonlinear HGODE on node- and graph-level benchmarks.
